title: Murder at the Rosewood Hotel
subtitle: Room 707, locked from the inside
briefing: Gerald Payne, a property developer, is found dead in room 707 at seven in the morning. The door is bolted from the inside and the window is sealed. The night manager opened it with the master key after Payne missed a car to the airport. There is one wine glass on the table where the room service docket says there should be two.
solution: Irene Falk was in the room as Payne's guest. She left through the connecting door to room 705, which she had booked under her maiden name, and bolted 707 from the inside by reaching through that connecting door before closing it. The missing second glass was in her own room. The elevator record that seemed to clear her only shows the main lift, not the service stair.

suspects.name: Irene Falk
suspects.motive: Stood to lose everything in the partnership dissolution Payne had filed.

statements.question: Where were you that night?
statements.text: In my own room from about midnight. I took the lift up at 11:50.

statements.question: There should be two glasses. Where is the second?
statements.text: How would I know? Perhaps housekeeping took it.

statements.question: Was the connecting door to 705 in use?
statements.text: It was locked. Those doors are always locked.

statements.question: When did you leave the hotel?
statements.text: At seven, like everyone else. I heard the commotion in the corridor.

suspects.name: Marcus Hale
suspects.motive: Payne had complained about him twice and wanted him dismissed.

statements.question: Where were you that night?
statements.text: At the desk. I did a floor check at one and again at three.

statements.question: There should be two glasses. Where is the second?
statements.text: The docket says two. I signed it myself. I cannot tell you where it went.

statements.question: Was the connecting door to 705 in use?
statements.text: 705 was occupied. I would have to check under what name.

statements.question: When did you leave the hotel?
statements.text: Seven fifteen, after the police arrived.

suspects.name: Dominic Vance
suspects.motive: Payne had him disciplined for an earlier complaint.

statements.question: Where were you that night?
statements.text: On the service floor. I took the order up at ten past one and came straight down.

statements.question: There should be two glasses. Where is the second?
statements.text: There were two on the tray. I set them both out. Somebody else moved one.

statements.question: Was the connecting door to 705 in use?
statements.text: It was ajar when I came in. I remember because it was odd.

statements.question: When did you leave the hotel?
statements.text: Six in the morning, end of shift.

suspects.name: Harriet Payne
suspects.motive: Inherits the controlling share of the family business.

statements.question: Where were you that night?
statements.text: In 512. I took a sleeping tablet at eleven and heard nothing.

statements.question: There should be two glasses. Where is the second?
statements.text: I was not in his room. I had not spoken to Gerald in a fortnight.

statements.question: When did you leave the hotel?
statements.text: I have not left. I am still here, being asked questions.

timeline.text: Irene takes the guest lift to the seventh floor.
Room service delivers one bottle and two glasses to 707.
The service attendant leaves the floor.
The service stair door is used once.
The connecting door between 707 and 705 is closed.
The night manager completes a floor check.
Room 707 is opened with the master key.

hints: A room bolted from inside is only impossible if there is one way in.
The docket says two glasses. Find the second one.
The guest lift is not the only way between floors.
